chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Meeting Armstrong in Chicago and the letter lost on the first airmail flight
summary: Taking Ory records to Chicago, Spikes met Louis Armstrong with King Oliver, and a letter he later sent Armstrong was lost on an air mail plane in 1932 and returned.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: It's that clipping you gave me from Gertrude [Gipson, Theatrical Editor of the Los Angeles Sentinel].

I just made these Kid Ory records, and I was taking them back to Chicago to try to get sales for 'em, you know--trying to promote the record, and when I got to Chicago, Louis [Armstrong] was playing there with King Oliver, and I met him and everything, and he said, "Well, Reb, one of these days, I'm going to be on a record. I'm going to try to make a record." He had never made a record.
And I showed you the letter I wrote him, and it was lost in the airplane.
Yeah. Right. It was stamped...marked...it was...

...was lost. That was the first...supposed to be the first mail plane from here to back East, and it was lost, and after come two, three years, they found the plane, and I guess they sent everybody the mail that was on there 'cause they sent me my letter back.
So you got this back, addressed to Louis Armstrong, and stamped from that flight. That's a really historical piece to have.
Yeah. Louis begged me for that. I said, "No, what am I gonna do without it?"
